process_facts.fact: Citation audit: every service then in the tool (203) had its Adobe source read and rated for how well it supports the service. 21 of these 60 Coworker services, CW00 included, were in that audit.

Outside review: two outside reviewers read the tool's catalog, which then held 31 of these 60 services. Each of their 223 claims was checked against the live Adobe page, and each claim that held went to a second checker told to refute it. That second check overturned or narrowed 18.
The Adobe quotes proposed for CW01 to CW07, CW-CJA, CW-AEM and CW-FSI were checked word for word against the live Adobe pages.
We read the 10 Adobe sources behind the Coworker case. 8 opened live. The 2 on business.adobe.com did not, because that site refuses automated tools, so we did not try again.
01:27 UTC: the owner pasted the Coworker answer from Adobe Support and Services (business.adobe.com). The Adobe Support and Services quote is checked against that paste.

04:43 UTC: the owner set the rule. List a Coworker service only when Adobe calls for the work directly, or the work follows from what Adobe documents about the feature, and give the citation for each one.

Two labels come from that rule. Adobe call-out: Adobe says a person, admin, developer or Adobe team must or should do the work. Follows from a documented feature: the work follows from a capability, limit, setting or data condition Adobe documents.

04:52 to 05:14 UTC: we read 286 Adobe pages live and saved each one. They cover all 80 pages in the Coworker guide's table of contents (8 hidden from its menu), the Coworker pages in 14 product guides, 5 Adobe news releases and 2 Adobe developer pages. All 286 returned HTTP 200; 5 more addresses returned 404 and were dropped.

From those pages we recorded 190 findings, each with an Adobe quote: 94 Adobe call-outs and 96 that follow from documented features. A script matched all 190 quotes word for word against the saved page text and the page HTML.

We proposed 26 new Coworker services. A separate skeptic review reread each one's Adobe page live (86 pages, 06:13 to 06:37 UTC) and checked its quote, its release status and its overlap with services already in the tool. 17 were corrected, 9 kept as written, none dropped.
07:29 UTC: the owner approved the 26 services, the Coworker + Adobe Analytics connection and six RFI write-ups.
08:20 UTC: the owner approved the industry-neutral wording, which renames CW-FSI to Coworker Skills for answer review.

We built the 26 into the SOW Builder and the RFI Builder in a working copy. A second skeptic review found no defects: the 26 match the approved record field by field, and all 67 service and connection quotes and all 189 RFI write-up quotes are on the Nov 17 page captures word for word. All 33 test suites pass.
With both approved changes saved, all 60 services are in the SOW Builder and 59 have an RFI Builder write-up. CW00, the shared setup on three Brand Visibility plays, is in the SOW Builder only.
Today the live tool has 34 of the 60 (repository commit 6a96c44, 06:14 UTC). The 26 new services and the CW-FSI rename are approved and built, and wait to be saved.
